title: region-aware-key-wrapping-and-rbac-hierarchy-for-tenant-chaining
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Introduce region-aware KMS wrapping and RBAC v2 hierarchical group support for tenant chaining. Adds audit translation to surface KMS location and tenant aliasing. Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag rbac_v2_tenant_chain.
description: Motivation: customers and regulators require cryptographic operations to be bounded to a tenant's configured region and for audit trails to include the resolved key location. Existing KMS scoping enforced at request time but allowed cross-region alias resolution for legacy keys; RBAC v1 lacks concise group inheritance semantics needed to model delegated tenant chains (service-account -> platform-broker -> tenant). This PR implements region-aware key wrapping, a tenant-scoped key alias migration path, and RBAC v2 hierarchical group checks to enable safe tenant chaining.
detailed_description:
Design summary:
- KMS region-aware wrapper: a thin platform-level component that resolves key aliases with tenant and region constraints, validates the key's location against the request's effective tenant region, and performs wrap/unwrap via the region-local KMS endpoint. For private deployments a configurable kms_region_map is respected. Errors contain auditable fields but do not leak sensitive key material.
- RBAC v2 hierarchical groups: policy evaluator extended to support group inheritance and explicit delegation chains. Policies may include a 'delegate_chain' clause that asserts which identity principals are allowed to perform operations on behalf of a tenant. This supports service accounts that act through platform brokers.
- Audit translation: audit exporter now enriches events with kms_key_region, key_alias_resolved, and tenant_chain if delegation occurred. These fields are surfaced in both internal logs and the tenant-facing audit bundles (redacted where necessary).
- Migration/tooling: migration tool (scripts/migrate-kms-aliases) to rewrite legacy global aliases into tenant-scoped aliases (format: tenant/<tenant-id>/key/<alias>) with safe fallback meta. The migration is idempotent and emits a report used by Governance teams.
- Feature flag & rollout: all runtime checks guarded by rbac_v2_tenant_chain and kms_region_enforce feature flags. We roll out in three phases: dry-run audit (collect only), soft-enforce for low-traffic tenants, and full enforce after 2 weeks with metrics stable.
Implementation notes:
- Changes touched: auth/policy/evaluator.go, kms/wrapper/region_wrapped_client.go, audit/exporter/translate.go, deploy/helm/values.yaml (private KMS maps), scripts/migrate-kms-aliases.py, docs/security/kms-region-and-delegation.md, tests/integration/kms_region_enforce_test.go.
- Performance: added a single network call for alias resolution when no cached mapping exists; integrated a short-lived platform cache with TTL=30s to remove observable p99 latency regressions. Benchmarks run in perf-canary show <1% token-latency impact for typical generation flows.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy aliases continue to work via the migration shim (reads prefer tenant-scoped alias if present), and the feature flag allows staged enforcement.
Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: policy evaluator inheritance tests (x8), kms wrapper happy/error paths (x12), audit enrichment cases (x6).
- Integration: e2e in staging exercise tenant-chained request path with private deployment (KMS emulator).
- Canary: canary rollout engaged for 5% of incoming requests with monitoring dashboards for fail rates and latency regressions.
Rollout & Monitoring:
- Dashboards: new panels for kms_key_region rejects, delegate_chain denials, migration report failures.
- Alerts: PagerDuty on >0.1% KMS-region-enforce rejects or sudden spike in delegate_chain errors.
- Rollback: flip off rbac_v2_tenant_chain and kms_region_enforce flags to revert runtime behavior; migration tool produces a reversal mapping to revert alias rewrites if needed.
Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: mis-migration could orphan keys — mitigated by idempotent migration with dry-run and multi-signer confirmation for write-phase.
- Risk: latency regression — mitigated with platform-side caching and canary limits.
Docs and compliance:
- Added docs/security/kms-region-and-delegation.md with example alias formats, operator migration steps, and FAQ for compliance teams.
- Updated privacy/audit-guidelines.md to describe new audit fields and retention considerations.

review_comments: Morgan Li: Please add a diagram for the delegate_chain flow and clarify the fallbacks when alias resolution fails.
Avery Chen: Added diagram to docs and clarified fallback semantics: if tenant-scoped alias unresolved we fall back to legacy alias only in dry-run; full-enforce mode rejects.
Diego Alvarez: Why introduce an in-memory TTL cache instead of leaning on existing runtime cache? Concern about duplication and consistency.

Avery Chen: TTL cache is a small platform-local cache to avoid cross-process coordination; we use existing distributed cache for long-lived mappings. Added comments and a helper to centralize cache instrumentation.
Priya Sharma: Tests look good, but add an integration test for private installer KMS map override.
Avery Chen: Added private-installer test and updated README with operator steps.
notes: Migration steps: 1) run scripts/migrate-kms-aliases.py --dry-run and review report; 2) schedule migration window and run without --dry-run; 3) enable rbac_v2_tenant_chain in dry-run audit mode for 48 hours; 4) enable soft-enforce for low-traffic tenants; 5) full-enforce after metrics stable. Governance must sign-off on final enforce step.
rollback_steps: Flip feature flags rbac_v2_tenant_chain and kms_region_enforce to false. Use migration tool report to map tenant aliases back to original global aliases if full revert necessary. Re-deploy previous helm values for private KMS map.
changelog_entry: Security: enforce tenant-region KMS wrapping and add RBAC v2 delegation chains (feature-flagged).
testing_summary: Unit and integration coverage added. Canary at 5% for 72h, then ramped to 20% before full rollout. No production rejects observed during canary; 2 migration warnings fixed pre-rollout.
